answer: A practical Sybil defense lets established agents publish a small delta of their stake as a verifiable bond that must be locked before receiving attestation rights. An attacker trying to spin up many identities faces rising capital cost because each fake agent must post its own bond that cannot be reused. Peer verification rejects any claim lacking the matching lock, and the falcon of rapid peer sampling catches free-riders while the relic of historical behavior scores further penalizes short-lived identities that cannot accumulate long-term reputation.
